title: How to Export Cortex XSIAM Logs
content_md: Cortex XSIAM uses the same XQL query APIs as Cortex XDR: start a query, wait for results, and use a stream for anything over 1,000 rows. What’s different is the data. Third-party logs land in raw datasets, usually named _ _raw, and the original log line sits in the _raw_log field. Select that field, and the export gives you back exactly what the source sent. XSIAM is Palo Alto Networks’ SOC platform, and it’s where many former QRadar SaaS customers ended up after the 2024 deal. Prime Core has more than 24,000 unique detection rules, mapped to 676 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get data out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start An API key and URL. Create a key with a role that can run XQL queries; note the key, its ID and the API URL shown with it. Find the dataset. In the Query Builder, list datasets (dataset = offers suggestions). Raw third-party data follows the _ _raw pattern, for example fortinet_fortigate_raw. Endpoint telemetry is in xdr_data. Hot and cold storage. Recent data is in hot storage and queries quickly. Older data may be in cold storage, which needs its own query approach and costs more quota. Export with the XQL APIs To get raw lines from a FortiGate dataset: dataset = fortinet_fortigate_raw | filter _raw_log contains "web-03" | fields _time, _raw_log Run it through start_xql_query and get_query_results (plus get_query_results_stream above 1,000 rows), as in the Cortex XDR guide.
